ratifications.statement: SUPERSEDED is a derived response state, not a disclosure_state value.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no locator, disclosure_state, or SUPERSEDED response-state model exists in the repository at HEAD; CAP-02/stella_0007 has no versioning or supersession concept at all (see superseded_authority_references.CAP_02_STELLA_0007).

ratifications.statement: A superseded locator returns the named version's complete safe public core. Successor identity/link is disclosed only when the successor is active and eligible for public disclosure.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no versioned-report/successor-linking model exists in the repository at HEAD.

ratifications.statement: REVOKED returns only revoked status and revocation date. No substantive report content is returned.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: PARTIALLY_CONSISTENT_AT_DESIGN_LEVEL_ONLY — CAP-02's unapplied design already models revocation via report_public_disclosures.revoked_at (revoked disclosures return zero rows, collapsed into the endpoint's generic 404, not a distinct REVOKED status/body). This ratification requires a distinct REVOKED response shape (status + revocation date, explicitly separated from NOT_FOUND per PVRI-04), which is NOT present in CAP-02's design and is NOT implemented anywhere at HEAD.

ratifications.statement: NOT_FOUND must collapse the observable response semantics for: unknown locator, not_disclosed, absent, ineligible, and other non-public cases, using the same status/body/public cache semantics. Literal constant-time processing must not be promised. Malformed tokens may reject before DB access. A useful timing oracle must not be deliberately introduced.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: PARTIALLY_CONSISTENT_AT_DESIGN_LEVEL_ONLY — CAP-02's verify_report RPC already collapses 'hash inexistente, reporte sin disclosure, disclosure revocada, borrador con disclosure' into one indistinguishable empty result set by construction of its JOIN (docs/ops/capabilities/CAP_02_PUBLIC_VERIFICATION.md section 4.1), and explicitly records the residual timing risk as RR-CAP-02-E (result is indistinguishable by construction; latency is not equalized or measured). This is consistent in spirit with PVRI-04's no-timing-oracle framing but predates and does not implement PVRI-04's REVOKED/NOT_FOUND split from PVRI-03, and no malformed-token pre-DB-access rejection is specified in CAP-02 beyond basic shape validation (section 7).

ratifications.statement: Public locator and integrity/content digest are permanently independent identifiers.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — CAP-02/stella_0007 uses a single identifier (verification_hash) as both lookup token and implicit content reference; no separate locator/digest pair exists in the repository at HEAD. This ratification supersedes that single-identifier model.

ratifications.statement: Integrity digest uses a governed explicit allow-list projection, RFC 8785/JCS canonicalization, UTF-8, SHA-256 lower-case hexadecimal. Numeric quantities in the canonical projection use canonical decimal-string semantics where defined by the projection. Ordering must be explicit. At least three test vectors must be frozen.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no JCS/RFC 8785 canonicalization, allow-list projection, or SHA-256 integrity digest mechanism exists in the repository at HEAD; this ratification is a forward specification with no frozen test vectors materialized yet (frozen test vectors are not authored by this docs-only materialization lane).

ratifications.statement: Locator is a 160-bit CSPRNG value, Crockford Base32 encoded, 32 uppercase canonical characters, with case-insensitive input normalization.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — CAP-02/stella_0007's verification_hash is a varchar(255) hash value, not a 160-bit CSPRNG Crockford-Base32 locator; no locator generation mechanism exists in the repository at HEAD.

ratifications.statement: Locator is immutable. Revocation kills that locator permanently. Any later reactivation/publication requires a new locator.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no locator lifecycle/immutability mechanism exists in the repository at HEAD; CAP-02's disclosure can be reinstated (report.disclosure.reinstated audit event, section 10) which is a different lifecycle than 'revocation kills the locator permanently, new publication needs a new locator' and would require rework under this ratification.

ratifications.statement: Rate limiting uses multiple dimensions, including a mandatory distinct-locator-per-IP counter. Any numeric thresholds proposed in the authority are INITIAL V1 DEFAULTS in governed/versioned operational configuration, not immutable product constants.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: PARTIALLY_CONSISTENT_AT_DESIGN_LEVEL_ONLY — CAP-02's design already proposes per-IP and global rate limits on /verify/* (docs/ops/capabilities/CAP_02_PUBLIC_VERIFICATION.md section 9: 30/min per IP, 600/min global), framed there as 'proposed' values, but it has no distinct-locator-per-IP counter dimension (it has no locator concept at all — see PVRI-05/PVRI-07) and is unapplied/unenabled at HEAD, so no rate limiting is live.

ratifications.statement: On shared limiter failure, the minimal public core page may deliberately fail open only to a bounded degraded in-process limiter. PDF/public_document delivery fails closed with 503. This deliberate fail-open requires independent security review before release.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no shared/degraded limiter tiering exists in the repository at HEAD. See required_independent_reviews above; this ratification's fail-open behavior is not to be implemented or released without the flagged review.

ratifications.statement: Implement a canonical /verify entry route with one locator field and one submit action that redirects to the canonical locator route.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no /verify entry route with a locator-submission form exists in the repository at HEAD; only app/(public)/verify/[hash]/page.tsx (direct hash-in-path access) and app/(public)/verify/[hash]/pdf/route.ts exist.

ratifications.statement: Rename the route semantic from [hash] to [locator]. No legacy redirect is required.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — the live route segment at HEAD is literally app/(public)/verify/[hash]/... ; renaming to [locator] is application-code work explicitly out of scope for this DOCS_ONLY materialization lane and is left to a future implementation lane.

ratifications.statement: Public verification surfaces require robots/noindex controls consistent with the authority's anti-indexing posture.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: FUTURE_MEASUREMENT_REQUIRED — whether app/(public)/verify/** currently emits noindex/robots controls was not re-measured by this docs-only materialization lane; not asserted here either way.

ratifications.statement: VALID and SUPERSEDED use the same HTTP cache policy per representation. REVOKED and NOT_FOUND must be strict no-store/no-cache. Maximum cached VALID-core revocation lag is 60 seconds. Contradictory cache-header prose must be removed or avoided.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no HTTP cache-policy differentiation by response state exists in the repository at HEAD for the /verify surface; CAP-02's design does not specify cache headers at all.

ratifications.statement: The internal rendered-artifact cache key must bind at minimum: content digest, representation kind, and renderer/version identity. Locator/disclosure identity is added only when it affects rendered bytes. This internal artifact cache must not be conflated with HTTP authorization/cache semantics.
ratifications.implementation_status_as_of_head: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no internal rendered-artifact cache exists for public verification content in the repository at HEAD.
